# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. export function projectType(root) {

    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)

# GitHub Actions Visual Workflow Editor

## Product idea

Build a browser-based visual editor for GitHub Actions YAML, tentatively called
**FlowForge**. Users design and understand workflows as connected nodes while
keeping the GitHub Actions YAML as the source of truth.

The product should be a workflow IDE rather than only a diagram generator:
visualize existing workflows, safely edit them, validate execution paths,
compare runs, generate workflows from natural-language goals, and collaborate
through pull requests and visual diffs.

## Core experience

- Import an existing `.github/workflows/*.yml` file.
- Render triggers, jobs, steps, dependencies, permissions, secrets, matrices,
  artifacts, and conditions as a flow diagram.
- Edit through node properties, inline YAML, or both side by side.
- Keep edits synchronized with the underlying YAML.
- Validate continuously with schema checks, expression checks, and `actionlint`.
- Explain execution order, skipped jobs, permissions, environment variables,
  and dependency paths.
- Preview a readable YAML diff before saving, committing, or opening a PR.

Example flow:

```text
Trigger
  ↓
Checkout
  ↓
Install dependencies
  ↓
Build ──────→ Upload artifact
  ↓
Test
  ↓
Deploy
```

## MVP

- Import and export GitHub Actions YAML.
- Visual job graph with collapsible steps.
- Add, delete, reorder, and connect jobs.
- Common action library for checkout, language setup, caching,
  artifact upload/download, Docker builds, and deployment.
- Editable `runs-on`, `if`, `needs`, `env`, `permissions`, action inputs, and
  secrets.
- Workflow dispatch and reusable workflow support.
- YAML diff preview and validation panel with actionable errors.
- Safe-mode warnings before changing triggers, permissions, secrets, or deploy
  steps.

## Differentiating features

- **Explain this workflow:** generate a plain-English description of each job
  and the overall pipeline.
- **Why was this skipped?:** trace `if` expressions, event filters, matrix
  behavior, and `needs` dependencies.
- **Runtime overlay:** import a GitHub Actions run and color graph nodes as
  passed, failed, skipped, cancelled, or in progress.
- **Visual pull-request diff:** show structural workflow changes, not only text
  changes.
- **Natural-language generation:** describe a goal, produce a visual draft,
  and require review before generating YAML.
- **Security linting:** flag excessive permissions, unpinned actions, exposed
  secrets, unsafe shell interpolation, and suspicious third-party actions.
- **Reusable workflow navigation:** make called workflows and composite actions
  clickable and inspectable.
- **Version history:** compare workflow graphs across commits and runs.

## Project-specific opportunity

The current OpenCode workflow is a good stress test because it includes:

- Multiple event triggers and conditional execution.
- Dynamic environment variables and issue-derived inputs.
- External repository checkouts.

export const CREATED_AT = 1793491200000
export const SAVE_VERSION = 7

function mulberry32(seed: number) {
  let a = seed >>> 0
  return () => {
    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0
    let t = a
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1)
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61)
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
  }
}

function history(price: number, volatility: number, seed: number, points = 64): number[] {
  const rand = mulberry32(seed)
  const out: number[] = []
  let value = price * (0.72 + rand() * 0.2)
  for (let i = 0; i < points; i += 1) {
    const drift = (price - value) * 0.035
    const noise = value * volatility * (rand() - 0.48) * 0.34
    value = Math.max(price * 0.08, value + drift + noise)
    out.push(Number(value.toFixed(value < 1 ? 6 : 2)))
  }
  out[out.length - 1] = price
  return out
}

function indexHistory(seed: number, points = 72): number[] {
  const rand = mulberry32(seed)
  const out: number[] = []
  let value = 3910
  for (let i = 0; i < points; i += 1) {
    value += 4.2 + (rand() - 0.47) * 42
    out.push(Number(value.toFixed(2)))
  }
  out[out.length - 1] = 4286.42
  return out
}

I made a type error: `kind: 'media' as FeedPost['kind']` but kind union doesn't include 'media'. It includes market, scandal, news, social, crime. Change to 'news' or add 'media' to union. Better add 'media' to FeedPost kind. Update types and remove cast. Let's do later.

Also `history` for player net worth generates values ending at 11.8M? The function sets last to price, but price passed 11.8M and volatility 0.02, starts 8.5M, ends 11.8M. Good.

Need net worth function. Create `lib/economy.ts` with calculations:
- tokenValue = sum holdings units*price + staked*price + pending
- ispValue = capacity*180000 + dataCenters*220000 + nodes*40000
- mediaValue = reach*600000*credibility/100 + shows*50000
- bankValue = playerOwned ? reserves + (deposits-loans)*? maybe reserves*0.8 + equity. Use max(0, reserves - (loans-deposits)*0.3) etc.
- districtValue = owned*value
- syndicateCash? dirty included separately.
- netWorth = cash + dirty*0.78 + token value + isp values (player) + media values (player) + bank equity + owned district values + legal fund - debts.
- portfolio allocation for chart.
- market cap.
- bank leverage = loans / max(reserves,1)
- isp utilization = load/capacity? load stored as 0-1 fraction of capacity. Actually load 0.62 means 62% utilization. Capacity 18. Revenue = capacity*load*price/24. Fine.
- media value.
- stock/company valuations? We don't have corporations separate; the asset empire is ISP/media/bank. Good enough. But prompt says corporations. Could add `corporations` state? Hmm. We have NPC companies via tokens and banks/media. Maybe add a "Corporations" section on dashboard with "Nihann Holdings" and rival corporations? But no stock trading. The spec asks corporate warfare. We could model "corporations" as a list with valuation, revenue, shares, owner, sector, and allow acquisition? That adds scope. Alternatively, treat media/ISP/bank as corporations. But "Corporate espionage" mechanic could be via hacking/exposé. Maybe add a `corporations` array with 6 companies and a "corporate raid" action? That would enrich. However, time. We can add `Corporation` type and seed, show in markets page as "Equities" tab with buy/sell shares. This is a significant feature but manageable. Let's consider.

```
Corporation { id, name, ticker, sector, valuation, sharePrice, sharesOutstanding, playerShares, npcOwner, revenue, growth, volatility, history, hue, description }
```

Player can buy/sell shares. Corporate raid: acquire >50% then collect dividend, hostile takeover. NPC actions affect stock. This adds another asset class. Dashboard can show "Equities" mini table. Markets page tabs: Tokens | Equities. Let's implement. It adds richness and is not too hard.

```
export interface Corporation { id, name, ticker, sector, ownerId, ownerName, sharePrice, sharesOutstanding, playerShares, revenue, growth, volatility, history, hue, description, control }
```
State `corporations: Corporation[]`.

export function generateLocalEvent(state: GameState): WorldEvent {
  const total = templates.reduce((sum, template) => sum + template.weight(state), 0)
  let roll = Math.random() * total
  let chosen = templates[0]
  for (const template of templates) {
    roll -= template.weight(state)
    if (roll <= 0) {
      chosen = template
      break
    }
  }
  const severityDays = chosen.severity === 'critical' ? 4 : chosen.severity === 'high' ? 6 : 8
  return {
    id: uid('evt'),
    title: chosen.title,
    description: chosen.description,
    category: chosen.category,
    severity: chosen.severity,
    startedDay: state.day,
    endsDay: state.day + severityDays,
    effects: chosen.effects(state),
    source: 'local',
    hue: chosen.hue,
    headline: chosen.headline,

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build the game described in the attached PDF, **OmniLife: The Syndicate**, as a working, deeply simulated economic MMO web game rather than a static prototype.
- The PDF asks for Next.js App Router, Tailwind, Supabase Realtime, Grok AI world engine, living city districts, ISP infrastructure, media networks, banking, crypto DEX, crime syndicate, government, social feed, and a god-mode backdoor for `mirajx132@gmail.com`.

## Requirements
- Follow the PDF prompt and make the game.
- Production-grade, no placeholders, no skipped files.
- Core systems requested: living city/property/crime, ISP fiber/data centers/bandwidth, TV/streaming/media manipulation, fractional-reserve banking/bank runs, AMM DEX/staking/rug pulls/flash loans, crime/laundering/bribery/hacking, government taxes/regulations/warrants/bailouts, server-wide social feed, Grok-powered autonomous NPCs, Unsplash imagery, god-mode admin terminal.
- UI must be responsive and visually polished.

## Decisions
- Built as Next.js static export served by a custom `server.mjs` that also provides `/api/world-engine`, `/api/health`, `/api/imagery`, `/api/npc-action`.
- Added a fully local deterministic/procedural simulation fallback so the game works without Supabase/Grok credentials.
- Grok is server-side only; the exact key from the PDF was placed in ignored `.env.local`, not committed.
- Added an equities market in addition to tokens to support corporate warfare.
- Default player email is `mirajx132@gmail.com`, so God Mode is visible by default; changing the profile email can revoke it.
- `start.sh` runs `npm run build`, writes `deployment-output.json` pointing at `out/`, then runs `node server.mjs`.
- `capture.sh` delegates to runtime `default-capture.mjs`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Extracted and read the 3-page PDF spec.
- Scaffolded Next.js 16 + React 19 + Tailwind 4 project and installed dependencies.
- Created simulation/state types, seeded world, economy helpers, world-event generator, tick simulation, and all player action functions.
- Created optional Grok client and server API integration.
- Created custom static/API server, build/start/capture scripts, `.env.example`, `.env.local`, and updated `.gitignore`.
- Created global neo-noir terminal styling and app layout.
- Created `GameProvider` with tick loop, localStorage persistence, toasts, engine health check, and world-event sync.
- Created `Shell` with sidebar, mobile drawer, topbar, ticker, notifications, profile modal, and toasts.
- Created reusable UI/chart primitives and the full Command Center dashboard.
- Created app route files for all pages.
- Created `MarketsPage` (tokens, equities, minting, trade terminal, staking, rug pull, flash loans, board raids).
- Created `BankingPage` (bank tables, deposits/withdrawals, loans, bank creation, rates, reserves, bank runs, contagion monitor).
- Created `InfrastructurePage` (topology map, ISP table, node/data-center builds, upgrades, repairs, security, rival hacking).
- Created `MediaPage` (network table, station detail, shows, propaganda, exposé, fake news, narrative market, gallery imagery).

### Active
- Need to create `UnderworldPage`, `GovernmentPage`, `WirePage`, `AdminPage`.
- Need to verify TypeScript/build, fix any compile/runtime errors, and run visual capture.
- Need to create Supabase schema and README updates.

### Blocked
- None currently.

## Next Move
1. Create `components/pages/Underworld.tsx` with heat, laundering, bribes, smuggling, racketeering, cyber heist, syndicate leaderboard, warrants, operations.
2. Create `components/pages/Government.tsx` with tax/regulation/approval, officials, bribery, lobbying, campaign funding, warrant dismissal, bailouts, regulations, warrants.
3. Create `components/pages/Wire.tsx` with full feed, player composer, filters, trending tags, sentiment.
4. Create `components/pages/Admin.tsx` with god-mode controls: spawn cash, pump/crash tokens, crash market, wipe entities, inject events, max influence, reset world.
5. Run `npm run lint` / `npm run build`, fix errors.
6. Start app and verify desktop/mobile screenshots via `capture.sh` or Playwright.
7. Add `supabase/schema.sql` with Users, Corporations, Banks, Tokens, ISP Networks, Media Stations, Crime Syndicates, SocialPosts, RLS, realtime publication, and AMM functions.
8. Update `README.md` with setup, architecture, env vars, and gameplay.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/types.ts`: all game state types.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/seed.ts`: initial world data, tokens, districts, banks, corporations, media, NPCs, events, feed.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/simulation.ts`: tick engine, NPC moves, bank runs, events, `advance`, `applyWorldEvent`, `forceBankRun`, `summarizeState`.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/actions.ts`: all player/god-mode actions.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/economy.ts`: net worth, allocation, daily income, leverage/risk, changes.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/world-events.ts`: local event templates and rumors.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/lib/grok.ts`: client engine health/event requests and sanitization.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/GameProvider.tsx`: state, tick loop, persistence, toasts.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/Shell.tsx`: navigation/layout/topbar/profile/notifications.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/ui.tsx`: panels, charts, gauges, donut, modal, tabs, badges.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/pages/Dashboard.tsx`: command center.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/pages/Markets.tsx`: markets/DEX/equities/mint.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/pages/Banking.tsx`: banking.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/pages/Infrastructure.tsx`: ISP/network.
- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/components/pages/Media.tsx`: media empire.

- `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann/app/globals.css`: theme/utilities/animations.

## Important Context
- Worktree is uncommitted; no commit or push has been made.
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/Nihann/Nihann`.
- Runtime requires `start.sh` to write `deployment-output.json` with `{ project, directory }` where `directory` contains `index.html`; static export `out/` satisfies this.
- `capture.sh` expects `RUNTIME_DIR`, `CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR`.
- Default god email: `mirajx132@gmail.com`.
- `.env.local` contains the PDF-provided `GROK_API_KEY` and is gitignored; preview will use local AI fallback unless the key is available.
- Next config uses `output: 'export'`, `trailingSlash: true`, `images.unoptimized`.
- `app/` route files already exist for `/`, `/markets`, `/banking`, `/infrastructure`, `/media`, `/underworld`, `/government`, `/wire`, `/admin`; the last four components are still missing.
- Potential issues to verify: TS imports/unused imports, `@/` alias resolution, Tailwind 4 classes, hydration randomness (already removed most `Math.random` from render except some page helper series are deterministic), and `AreaChart` prop typing.

407: export function repayLoan(previous: GameState, bankId: string, amount: number): ActionResult {
408:   const state = clone(previous)
409:   const bank = state.banks.find((item) => item.id === bankId)
410:   const debt = state.player.debts[bankId] ?? 0
411:   if (!bank) return fail(previous, 'BANK NOT FOUND', 'This institution is not on the mesh.')
412:   if (amount <= 0 || debt <= 0) return fail(previous, 'NOTHING TO REPAY', 'There is no outstanding debt at this institution.')
413:   const payment = Math.min(amount, debt, state.player.cash)

416:   state.player.debts[bankId] = Math.max(0, debt - payment)
417:   bank.loans = Math.max(0, bank.loans - payment)
418:   bank.reserves += payment
419:   state.player.actions += 1
420:   log(state, `Repaid ${Math.round(payment).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD to ${bank.name}.`)
421:   return ok(state, 'DEBT SERVICED', `${Math.round(payment).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD repaid.`)
422: }

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build the game described in the attached PDF, **OmniLife: The Syndicate**, as a working, deeply simulated economic MMO web game rather than a static prototype.
- The PDF asks for Next.js App Router, Tailwind, Supabase Realtime, Grok AI world engine, living city districts, ISP infrastructure, media networks, banking, crypto DEX, crime syndicate, government, social feed, and a god-mode backdoor for `mirajx132@gmail.com`.

## Requirements
- Follow the PDF prompt and make the game.
- Production-grade, no placeholders, no skipped files.
- Core systems requested: living city/property/crime, ISP fiber/data centers/bandwidth, TV/streaming/media manipulation, fractional-reserve banking/bank runs, AMM DEX/staking/rug pulls/flash loans, crime/laundering/bribery/hacking, government taxes/regulations/warrants/bailouts, server-wide social feed, Grok-powered autonomous NPCs, Unsplash imagery, god-mode admin terminal.
- UI must be responsive and visually polished.

## Decisions
- Built as Next.js static export served by custom `server.mjs` with `/api/world-engine`, `/api/health`, `/api/imagery`, `/api/npc-action`.
- Added fully local deterministic/procedural simulation fallback so the game works without Supabase/Grok credentials.
- Grok is server-side only; the PDF key lives in ignored `.env.local`, not committed.
- Added equities market alongside tokens to support corporate warfare.
- Default player email is `mirajx132@gmail.com`, so God Mode is visible by default; changing profile email revokes it.
- `start.sh` runs build, writes `deployment-output.json` pointing at `out/`, then runs `node server.mjs`.
- `capture.sh` delegates to runtime `default-capture.mjs`.
- Added optional Supabase Realtime wire sync via `lib/supabase.ts`; local-first behavior remains when env vars are absent.
- Seed player influence changed from 120 to 100 to match 0–100 UI semantics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Extracted/read the 3-page PDF spec.
- Scaffolded Next.js 16 + React 19 + Tailwind 4 project and installed dependencies.
- Created simulation/state types, seeded world, economy helpers, world-event generator, tick simulation, and all player/god actions.
- Created optional Grok client and server API integration.
- Created custom static/API server, build/start/capture scripts, `.env.example`, `.env.local`, and updated `.gitignore`.
- Created global neo-noir terminal styling and app layout.
- Created `GameProvider` with tick loop, localStorage persistence, toasts, engine health check, world-event sync.
- Created `Shell` with sidebar, mobile drawer, topbar, ticker, notifications, profile modal, toasts.
- Created reusable UI/chart primitives and full Command Center dashboard.
- Created app route files for all pages.
- Created `MarketsPage`, `BankingPage`, `InfrastructurePage`, `MediaPage`.
- Created `UnderworldPage` with heat signature, laundering, smuggling, racketeering, cyber heist, syndicate board, bribery network, legal/warrant panel, operations log.
- Created `GovernmentPage` with policy pulse, officials grid, lobbying/campaign/bailout operations, regulations, warrants, budget/capture donut, council watch.
- Created `WirePage` with composer, filters/search, live feed, trending tags, top voices, sentiment monitor, protocol panel.
- Created `AdminPage` with root console, cash spawning, total capture, event injection, market crash, token pump/crash, entity wiper, world overview, root status, audit trail, guarded world reset.
- Fixed pre-existing `heatLabel` import errors in `Shell.tsx` and `Underworld.tsx`.
- Fixed `godCrashMarket` WorldEvent typing in `lib/actions.ts`.
- `npm run lint` / `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `npm run build` passes; static export generated for all 11 routes.
- Captured and visually inspected desktop + mobile screenshots for all 9 pages; no console/page/HTTP errors.
- Playwright interaction tests pass for laundering, bribery, lobbying, Wire posting, god cash spawn, event injection, token buy, bank deposit, node build, show launch, and mobile nav.
- Fixed Wire filter/search layout so tabs no longer clip against search.
- Created `lib/supabase.ts` with optional client, `publishWirePost`, and `subscribeToWire`.

### Active
- Integrate `subscribeToWire` into `GameProvider`.
- Call `publishWirePost` from `postToWire` (make `post()` helper return the created `FeedPost`).
- Create `supabase/schema.sql` with Users, Corporations, Banks, Tokens, ISP Networks, Media Stations, Crime Syndicates, SocialPosts, RLS, realtime publication, AMM functions.
- Add unit tests so `npm test` works.
- Update `README.md` with setup, architecture, env vars, Supabase setup, gameplay, god mode.
- Re-run lint/build/tests after Supabase integration and finalize screenshots if needed.

### Blocked
- None currently.

## Next Move
1. Modify `lib/actions.ts`: make the `post()` helper return the created `FeedPost`; in `postToWire`, capture it and call `void publishWirePost(item)`.
2. Modify `components/GameProvider.tsx`: import `subscribeToWire`; add a mount effect that prepends remote posts by unique id and caps feed at 70; keep `stateRef` in sync.
3. Create `supabase/schema.sql` with all core tables, RLS policies, indexes, `updated_at` trigger, `social_posts` realtime publication, and AMM swap function/pool table.
4. Add `tests/*.test.ts` covering economy, format, simulation, and deterministic actions; run `npm test`.
5. Update `README.md` while preserving the OMGithub marker block; document local mode, Grok, Supabase, scripts, systems, god mode, and deployment.
6. Run `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`; restart server and re-run interaction/capture checks.

356:   if (amount > previous.player.cash) return fail(previous, 'INSUFFICIENT CASH', 'Your liquid balance cannot cover this deposit.')
357:   const state = clone(previous)
358:   const bank = state.banks.find((item) => item.id === bankId)
359:   if (!bank) return fail(previous, 'BANK NOT FOUND', 'This institution is not on the mesh.')
360:   if (bank.status === 'collapsed') return fail(previous, 'BANK CLOSED', 'This bank has collapsed. Deposits are frozen.')
361:   state.player.cash -= amount
362:   state.player.deposits[bankId] = (state.player.deposits[bankId] ?? 0) + amount
363:   bank.deposits += amount
364:   bank.reserves += amount * 0.9
365:   state.player.actions += 1
366:   log(state, `Deposited ${Math.round(amount).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD into ${bank.name}.`)
367:   return ok(state, 'DEPOSIT CLEARED', `${Math.round(amount).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD deposited at ${bank.rate.toFixed(1)}% APR.`)
368: }

370: export function withdraw(previous: GameState, bankId: string, amount: number): ActionResult {
371:   const state = clone(previous)
372:   const bank = state.banks.find((item) => item.id === bankId)
373:   if (!bank) return fail(previous, 'BANK NOT FOUND', 'This institution is not on the mesh.')
374:   const balance = state.player.deposits[bankId] ?? 0
375:   if (amount <= 0 || amount > balance) return fail(previous, 'INVALID WITHDRAWAL', 'Choose an amount within your deposit.')
376:   if (bank.status === 'collapsed') return fail(previous, 'DEPOSITS FROZEN', 'A receiver has frozen this bank. Withdrawals are unavailable.')
377:   const available = Math.min(amount, bank.reserves * 0.92)
378:   if (available < 1) return fail(previous, 'RESERVES EXHAUSTED', 'The bank cannot honor a withdrawal right now. This is how runs begin.')
379:   state.player.cash += available
380:   state.player.deposits[bankId] = balance - available
381:   bank.deposits -= available
382:   bank.reserves -= available
383:   state.player.actions += 1
384:   log(state, `Withdrew ${Math.round(available).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD from ${bank.name}.`)
385:   return ok(state, 'WITHDRAWAL CLEARED', `${Math.round(available).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD returned to liquid cash.`)
386: }

388: export function takeLoan(previous: GameState, bankId: string, amount: number): ActionResult {
389:   if (amount <= 0) return fail(previous, 'INVALID LOAN', 'Enter a positive loan amount.')
390:   const state = clone(previous)
391:   const bank = state.banks.find((item) => item.id === bankId)
392:   if (!bank) return fail(previous, 'BANK NOT FOUND', 'This institution is not on the mesh.')
393:   if (bank.status === 'collapsed') return fail(previous, 'BANK CLOSED', 'This bank cannot underwrite new credit.')
394:   const capacity = Math.min(bank.reserves * 0.45, netWorth(state) * 0.45)
395:   if (amount > capacity) return fail(previous, 'UNDERWRITING REFUSED', `This institution can extend at most ${Math.round(capacity / 1000)}K against your balance sheet.`)
396:   bank.loans += amount
397:   bank.reserves -= amount
398:   state.player.cash += amount
399:   state.player.debts[bankId] = (state.player.debts[bankId] ?? 0) + amount
400:   state.player.heat = clamp(state.player.heat + 2, 0, 100)
401:   syncHeat(state)
402:   state.player.actions += 1
403:   log(state, `Borrowed ${Math.round(amount).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD from ${bank.name} at ${bank.rate.toFixed(1)}%.`)
404:   return ok(state, 'CREDIT FACILITY OPEN', `${Math.round(amount).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD borrowed at ${bank.rate.toFixed(1)}% APR.`)
405: }

407: export function repayLoan(previous: GameState, bankId: string, amount: number): ActionResult {
408:   const state = clone(previous)
409:   const bank = state.banks.find((item) => item.id === bankId)
410:   const debt = state.player.debts[bankId] ?? 0
411:   if (!bank) return fail(previous, 'BANK NOT FOUND', 'This institution is not on the mesh.')
412:   if (amount <= 0 || debt <= 0) return fail(previous, 'NOTHING TO REPAY', 'There is no outstanding debt at this institution.')
413:   const payment = Math.min(amount, debt, state.player.cash)
414:   if (payment <= 0) return fail(previous, 'INSUFFICIENT CASH', 'Your liquid balance cannot cover this payment.')
415:   state.player.cash -= payment
416:   state.player.debts[bankId] = Math.max(0, debt - payment)
417:   bank.loans = Math.max(0, bank.loans - payment)
418:   bank.reserves += payment
419:   state.player.actions += 1
420:   log(state, `Repaid ${Math.round(payment).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD to ${bank.name}.`)
421:   return ok(state, 'DEBT SERVICED', `${Math.round(payment).toLocaleString('en-US')} USD repaid.`)
422: }

20: function mulberry32(seed: number) {
21:   let a = seed >>> 0
22:   return () => {
23:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0
24:     let t = a
25:     t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1)
26:     t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61)
27:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
28:   }
29: }

31: function history(price: number, volatility: number, seed: number, points = 64): number[] {
32:   const rand = mulberry32(seed)
33:   const out: number[] = []
34:   let value = price * (0.72 + rand() * 0.2)
35:   for (let i = 0; i < points; i += 1) {
36:     const drift = (price - value) * 0.035
37:     const noise = value * volatility * (rand() - 0.48) * 0.34
38:     value = Math.max(price * 0.08, value + drift + noise)
39:     out.push(Number(value.toFixed(value < 1 ? 6 : 2)))
40:   }
41:   out[out.length - 1] = price
42:   return out
43: }

43: function effectValue(state: GameState, kind: EventEffect['kind'], targetId?: string): number {
44:   return state.events
45:     .filter((event) => event.endsDay >= state.day)
46:     .reduce((total, event) => {
47:       const matching = event.effects.filter(
48:         (effect) => effect.kind === kind && (!effect.targetId || effect.targetId === targetId),
49:       )
50:       return total + matching.reduce((sum, effect) => sum + effect.delta, 0)
51:     }, 0)
52: }

323: function tickTokens(state: GameState) {
324:   const marketEffect = effectValue(state, 'market')
325:   const playerHoldings = new Map(state.player.holdings.map((holding) => [holding.tokenId, holding]))
326:   for (const token of state.tokens) {

328:       token.price = Math.max(0.000001, token.price * 0.985)
329:       token.history.push(Number(token.price.toFixed(token.price < 1 ? 6 : 2)))
330:       if (token.history.length > MAX_HISTORY) token.history.shift()
331:       continue
332:     }
333:     const eventDelta = eventForToken(state, token.id)
334:     const meanReversion = ((token.fairValue - token.price) / Math.max(token.price, 0.000001)) * 0.006
335:     const noise = normalRandom() * token.volatility * 0.075
336:     const momentum = token.momentum * 0.36
337:     const total = meanReversion + noise + momentum + eventDelta * 0.11 + marketEffect * 0.55
338:     const change = clamp(total, -0.16, 0.16)
339:     token.price = Math.max(0.000001, token.price * (1 + change))
340:     token.momentum = clamp(token.momentum * 0.84 + normalRandom() * token.volatility * 0.05 + eventDelta * 0.04, -0.18, 0.18)
341:     token.fairValue = Math.max(0.000001, token.fairValue * (1 + normalRandom() * 0.004 + eventDelta * 0.03))
342:     token.volume24h = Math.max(10_000, token.volume24h * (0.96 + Math.random() * 0.09) + Math.abs(change) * token.liquidity * 0.4)
343:     token.holders = Math.max(100, Math.round(token.holders * (1 + (Math.random() - 0.48) * 0.006)))
344:     token.staked = Math.max(0, token.staked * (1 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.01))
345:     token.history.push(Number(token.price.toFixed(token.price < 1 ? 6 : 2)))
346:     if (token.history.length > MAX_HISTORY) token.history.shift()
347: 
348:     const holding = playerHoldings.get(token.id)
349:     if (holding && holding.staked > 0) {
350:       holding.pending += (holding.staked * token.price * (token.apr / 100)) / (365 * 24)
351:     }
352:   }
353: }

import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { test } from 'node:test'
import {
  allocation,
  bankRisk,
  dailyIncome,
  debtValue,
  heatLabel,
  leverage,
  netWorth,
  portfolioValue,
  tokenChange,
} from '../lib/economy'
import { clamp, clock, money, pct, tokenPrice, trendOf } from '../lib/format'
import { createInitialState } from '../lib/seed'

test('format helpers render money, prices, percentages and clocks', () => {
  assert.equal(money(1_234, true), '$1.2K')
  assert.equal(money(-1_234, true), '-$1.2K')
  assert.equal(money(2_500_000), '$2,500,000')
  assert.equal(tokenPrice(142.3), '$142.30')
  assert.equal(tokenPrice(0.0842), '$0.0842')
  assert.equal(tokenPrice(0.0001234), '$0.000123')
  assert.equal(pct(2.345), '+2.3%')
  assert.equal(pct(-4.2), '-4.2%')
  assert.equal(clock(42, 13), 'DAY 042 · 01:00 PM')
  assert.equal(clamp(120, 0, 100), 100)
  assert.equal(trendOf([100, 110, 121]), 21)
})

test('seeded world has the expected living systems', () => {
  const state = createInitialState()
  assert.equal(state.version, 7)
  assert.equal(state.districts.length, 10)
  assert.ok(state.tokens.length >= 6)
  assert.ok(state.banks.length >= 4)
  assert.ok(state.isps.some((isp) => isp.playerOwned))
  assert.ok(state.media.some((station) => station.playerOwned))
  assert.ok(state.syndicates.some((syndicate) => syndicate.playerOwned))
  assert.equal(state.player.godMode, true)
  assert.equal(state.player.influence, 100)
})

test('net worth and allocation account for the player portfolio', () => {
  const state = createInitialState()
  const worth = netWorth(state)
  assert.ok(Number.isFinite(worth))
  assert.ok(worth > 0)
  assert.equal(debtValue(state), 0)
  assert.ok(portfolioValue(state) > 0)

  const slices = allocation(state)
  assert.ok(slices.length >= 5)
  assert.ok(slices.every((slice) => slice.value > 0))
  assert.ok(dailyIncome(state) >= 0)
})

test('bank leverage and risk reflect the seeded loan book', () => {
  const state = createInitialState()
  const blackVault = state.banks.find((bank) => bank.id === 'blackvault')
  assert.ok(blackVault)
  assert.ok(Math.abs(leverage(blackVault!) - 728 / 64) < 1e-9)
  assert.equal(bankRisk(blackVault!) > 50, true)
  assert.equal(bankRisk(state.banks[0]) >= 0, true)
  assert.equal(bankRisk(state.banks[0]) <= 100, true)
})

test('heat labels map to the expected severity bands', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(heatLabel(10), { label: 'COOL', tone: 'good' })
  assert.deepEqual(heatLabel(30), { label: 'WARM', tone: 'warn' })
  assert.deepEqual(heatLabel(55), { label: 'HOT', tone: 'warn' })
  assert.deepEqual(heatLabel(90), { label: 'BURNING', tone: 'bad' })
})

test('token change is measured against recent history', () => {
  const state = createInitialState()
  const token = state.tokens[0]
  const change = tokenChange(token, 12)
  assert.ok(Number.isFinite(change))
  assert.equal(tokenChange({ ...token, history: [] }), 0)
})

# Nihann

<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->
## 🚀 Build, play, and remix with OMGithub

**Remixed using [OMGithub.com](https://omgithub.com).**

[![OMGithub](https://img.shields.io/badge/OMGithub-Open%20project-orange?style=for-the-badge)](https://omgithub.com/nihanalonee/Nihann)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source-181717?logo=github&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/nihanalonee/Nihann)

- 🎮 [Open the project](https://omgithub.com/nihanalonee/Nihann).
- ✨ [Remix this project](https://omgithub.com/?remix=nihanalonee%2FNihann).
- 💻 [Explore the source](https://github.com/nihanalonee/Nihann).
- 🛠️ [Check build runs](https://github.com/nihanalonee/Nihann/actions).
- 🐛 [Report an issue](https://github.com/nihanalonee/Nihann/issues).
- 👤 [Explore the creator's projects](https://omgithub.com/nihanalonee).
- 🌍 [Create with OMGithub](https://omgithub.com).
- 🧬 [Explore the remix source](https://github.com/nihanalonee/Nihann).
<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

---

## OmniLife: The Syndicate

A living economic MMO simulation set in the neon-soaked city of OmniLife. You run a
holding company, an ISP, a streaming network, a syndicate, and a growing political
operation. Every three seconds the world ticks: markets reprice, NPCs move, banks
strain, regulators react, and the Wire fills with rumor, scandal, and propaganda.

The simulation is **local-first**. It runs entirely in the browser with deterministic
seeding, procedural world events, and a full action economy. Grok and Supabase are
optional amplifiers, never hard dependencies.

### Feature map

| Module | What it simulates |
| --- | --- |
| **Command Center** | Net worth, allocation, market index, heat, event feed, district map, NPC roster |
| **Markets** | Token AMM trading, staking and rewards, token minting, rug pulls, flash loans, equities, board raids |
| **Banking** | Fractional-reserve deposits, withdrawals, credit lines, bank founding, reserve injection, bank runs, bailouts |
| **Infrastructure** | Fiber nodes, data centers, backbone upgrades, pricing, security, cyber intrusions, uptime and congestion |
| **Media** | Network launches, shows, propaganda campaigns, exposés, fabricated stories, reach and credibility |
| **Underworld** | Laundering, smuggling, racketeering, cyber heists, syndicate board, bribery, legal defense, warrants |
| **Government** | Policy pulse, lobbying, campaign funding, bailouts, regulations, warrants, budget and capture |
| **The Wire** | Server-wide social feed, posting, filters, trending tags, sentiment monitor, optional Supabase Realtime |
| **Admin** | God-mode root console: liquidity spawning, total capture, event injection, market crashes, token pumps, entity wipes, world reset |

### Tech stack

- **Next.js 16** App Router with a fully static export (`output: 'export'`)
- **React 19** and **TypeScript** in strict mode
- **Tailwind CSS 4** with a custom neo-noir terminal design system
- **lucide-react** iconography
- **Supabase** (optional) for durable profiles, shared Wire posts, and AMM SQL
- **Grok** (optional, server-side only) for autonomous world events
- **Node.js** custom server for the static build plus API routes
- **node:test + tsx** for unit tests

---

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:3000
```

Production-style run (builds the static export, writes the deployment manifest,
then serves it with the custom server):

```bash
npm start            # equivalent to ./start.sh
```

Or run the pieces directly:

```bash
npm run build        # static export into ./out
node server.mjs      # serves ./out and the API endpoints
```

The default profile is `mirajx132@gmail.com`, which means **God Mode is unlocked on
first boot**. Change the email in the profile modal to revoke it.

### Scripts

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Next dev server |
| `npm run build` | Static export to `out/` |
| `npm start` | `node server.mjs` (serves `out/` + APIs) |
| `npm test` | Unit tests (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts`) |
| `npm run lint` | TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| `./start.sh` | Install if needed, build, write `deployment-output.json`, serve |
| `./capture.sh` | Runtime screenshot hook; requires `RUNTIME_DIR`, `CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR` |

`start.sh` writes `deployment-output.json` with `{ project, directory }`, where
`directory` points at the static export (`out/`). The runtime uses that manifest to
serve the game.

---

## Environment variables

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in only what you need. The game boots
and plays with none of them.

```bash
# Server-only Grok credentials. Never use a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.
GROK_API_KEY=
GROK_MODEL=grok-3-mini

# Optional: enables live Supabase Realtime Wire sync.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=

# Optional: enables live Unsplash imagery in the media module.
UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY=
```

- **`GROK_API_KEY`** is read only by `server.mjs`. The browser calls `/api/world-engine`;
  the key never reaches the client. Without it, the server returns a locally generated
  event and the UI shows `LOCAL AI`.
- **Supabase** is optional. Without it, the Wire is fully local and persisted in
  `localStorage`. With it, posts are mirrored to `social_posts` and remote posts arrive
  over Realtime.
- **Unsplash** is optional. Without it, the imagery endpoint returns curated gradient
  placeholders.

`.env.local` is gitignored. Do not commit keys.

---

## Supabase setup

1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2. Open the SQL editor and run [`supabase/schema.sql`](supabase/schema.sql).
3. Enable **Realtime** for `public.social_posts` (the schema adds it to the
   `supabase_realtime` publication).
4. Copy the project URL and anon key into `.env.local`:

   ```bash
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://YOUR-PROJECT.supabase.co
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR-ANON-KEY
   ```

5. Rebuild (`npm run build`) so the public env vars are baked into the client bundle.

The schema includes:

- `profiles` with an `auth.users` trigger that creates a profile automatically
- `corporations`, `banks`, `tokens`, `isp_networks`, `media_stations`,
  `crime_syndicates`
- `social_posts` with author-bound RLS and Realtime
- `liquidity_pools` plus a locked constant-product `amm_swap(token, amount, direction)`
  function
- Public-read / owner-write RLS policies and `updated_at` triggers
- Seed rows matching the local world

> **Auth note:** Wire inserts require an authenticated Supabase session because RLS
> binds `author_id` to `auth.uid()`. When no session exists, the local post still
> succeeds and the remote mirror is skipped silently.

---

## Grok world engine

The browser periodically posts a compact world snapshot to `/api/world-engine`. The
server asks Grok for a single structured event and validates it before returning:

```json
{
  "title": "Liquidity Crisis",
  "description": "A clearing house missed margin at the open...",
  "category": "finance",
  "severity": "high",
  "headline": "LIQUIDITY CRISIS: interbank lending freezes",
  "hue": 350,
  "effects": [
    { "kind": "market", "delta": -0.012 },
    { "kind": "token", "targetId": "luna", "delta": -0.018 }
  ]
}
```

If Grok is unavailable, times out, or returns malformed JSON, the endpoint falls back
to the local event generator. The simulation never blocks on the network.

### API endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/health` | `GET` | Reports server and Grok configuration status |
| `/api/world-engine` | `POST` | Generates or falls back to a world event |
| `/api/npc-action` | `POST` | Produces a contextual NPC action |
| `/api/imagery` | `GET` | Unsplash-backed media imagery with gradient fallback |

---

## Gameplay loop

1. **Build the balance sheet.** Trade tokens, stake yield, buy equities, acquire
   district deeds, and expand AetherLink capacity.
2. **Manufacture attention.** Launch shows, run propaganda, publish exposés, and
   post to the Wire to move sentiment and price.
3. **Capture the state.** Lobby City Hall, fund campaigns, bribe officials, and
   request bailouts when the system is too big to fail.
4. **Manage heat.** Launder dirty cash, bribe the FCU, fund legal defense, or dismiss
   warrants before they are served.
5. **Survive the consequences.** Bank runs, cyber intrusions, regulatory crackdowns,
   market crashes, and hostile NPC moves all feed back into the same economy.

Every action is evaluated against the current world state and produces a toast,
notification, log entry, and sometimes a Wire post. The simulation autosaves to
`localStorage` under `omnilife.syndicate.save.v7`; the Admin page can reseed the world.

### God mode

God mode is bound to `mirajx132@gmail.com`. Open the profile modal from the topbar,
confirm the email, and the **Admin** route becomes available. The console supports:

- spawning liquid and dirty cash
- total political capture (influence, reputation, officials, warrants)
- injecting a world event
- crashing the entire market
- pumping or crashing any token
- wiping a bank, ISP, media network, or corporation
- a guarded world reset

Changing the profile email away from the admin address revokes access immediately.

---

## Architecture

```text
app/                      Next.js routes (static export)
  page.tsx                Command Center
  markets/ banking/ infrastructure/ media/
  underworld/ government/ wire/ admin/
  layout.tsx              Root layout + metadata
  globals.css             Design tokens and terminal styling

components/
  GameProvider.tsx        State, tick loop, persistence, toasts, engine sync, Realtime
  Shell.tsx               Sidebar, mobile drawer, topbar, ticker, profile modal
  ui.tsx                  Panels, charts, gauges, donut, modal, tabs, badges
  pages/                  One component per route

lib/
  types.ts                All domain types
  seed.ts                 Deterministic seeded world
  simulation.ts           Tick engine, NPC AI, bank runs, warrants, events
  actions.ts              Every player and god action
  economy.ts              Net worth, allocation, leverage, risk, income
  world-events.ts         Procedural event templates and rumors
  grok.ts                 Browser-side engine client
  supabase.ts             Optional client, publish, Realtime subscription
  format.ts               Money, time, number, color helpers

server.mjs                Static server + Grok/API routes
supabase/schema.sql       Tables, RLS, Realtime, AMM
tests/                    Unit tests for economy, simulation, actions
```

### State model

`GameState` is a single serializable tree: player, districts, tokens, banks,
corporations, ISPs, media, syndicates, government, feed, events, NPCs, and market
aggregates. `advance(state)` clones the tree, runs the subsystem ticks in order, and
returns the next state. Actions clone too, so React state updates remain predictable
and testable.

### Persistence

- Local save: `localStorage`, debounced 500 ms, versioned by `SAVE_VERSION`.
- Remote Wire: Supabase `social_posts`, merged by post `id` to avoid double-rendering
  your own echoed transmission.

---

## Tests

```bash
npm test
```

Coverage includes formatting, seeded-world invariants, net worth and allocation,
bank leverage/risk, heat bands, tick immutability, day rollover, forced bank runs,
world-event application, token buys/sells, deposits/withdrawals, Wire posting, god
gating, profile-based god mode, and ISP expansion.

---

## Deployment

The project builds to static HTML/CSS/JS in `out/` and is served by `server.mjs`,
which also hosts the API routes. `start.sh` performs the full pipeline:

```bash
./start.sh
```

For a platform that expects a manifest, `start.sh` writes:

```json
{
  "project": "/absolute/path/to/project",
  "directory": "/absolute/path/to/project/out"
}
```

Set `PORT` to choose the listening port (default `3000`). Set
`NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` to silence Next telemetry.

---

## Design notes

- **Neo-noir terminal:** deep navy/black surfaces, cyan and magenta accents, amber
  warnings, rose failures, thin borders, and dense monospace numerics.
- **Responsive:** sidebar collapses into a mobile drawer; cards, charts, and tables
  reflow at small widths.
- **No placeholders:** every route, action, and subsystem is implemented. Optional
  integrations degrade to deterministic local behavior instead of empty states.
- **Server-side secrets:** Grok and Unsplash keys stay in `server.mjs`; only public
  Supabase configuration is exposed to the client.
